This impact is significantly higher than previous estimates that only considered temperature increases and average precipitation.

brief.context: France utilizes a two-round electoral system, which currently appears poised to force a choice between far-right and far-left candidates. This dynamic has created an 'orphan electorate' among centrists who feel alienated by the current political polarization.
brief.why: According to Jean-Daniel Lévy of Toluna France, centrists are afraid of a duel between political extremes. Raphaël LLorca of the Jean-Jaurès Foundation suggests the search for new candidates reflects a broader panic within the centrist bloc as the election slips away from them.
brief.next: Voters will head to the polls in the spring to choose a successor to President Emmanuel Macron.

items.title: Onitsuka Tiger owner Asics shares slide as sales growth slows
items.summary: Shares of Asics, the parent company of Onitsuka Tiger, declined as investors reacted to concerns that the brand's recent sales momentum is decelerating. Analysts are now questioning whether the company can meet its established annual performance targets.

brief.what: Asics shares experienced a decline following market concerns regarding a slowdown in the company's sales growth.
brief.who: Asics, the owner of the Onitsuka Tiger brand, is the primary subject, while market analysts are the entities expressing concern over the company's financial trajectory.
brief.context: Asics has previously been identified as a standout performer within the athleisure sector, a market segment that has seen significant growth.
brief.why: Analysts fear that the recent deceleration in sales growth may prevent the company from achieving its annual targets.

items.title: How fat are AI trading bots’ fingers?
items.summary: The article examines the potential risks associated with AI-driven trading bots and the implications of their automated decision-making processes in financial markets.

brief.what: The report investigates the operational risks posed by AI trading bots, specifically focusing on the potential for errors or 'fat-finger' mistakes within automated systems.
brief.who: The Financial Times serves as the primary reporter analyzing these market risks.
brief.context: Automated trading systems have become increasingly prevalent in modern financial markets, necessitating a closer look at their reliability and the consequences of algorithmic failures.
brief.why: The investigation was prompted by the need to size up the risks inherent in deploying artificial intelligence for high-speed financial transactions.

items.title: Chinese AI sell-off deepens over fears of tougher Nvidia chip restrictions
items.summary: Chinese artificial intelligence stocks are declining amid growing concerns regarding potential new restrictions on Nvidia chip exports. The market reaction follows reports that Nvidia's leadership previously advocated for maintaining open sales to the Chinese market.

brief.what: Chinese AI-related stocks are experiencing a deepened sell-off as investors react to fears of stricter limitations on the export of Nvidia chips to China.
brief.who: Nvidia, the chip manufacturer, and its chief executive Jensen Huang are central to the narrative regarding trade access.
brief.context: The technology sector is currently navigating complex geopolitical tensions that impact the supply chain of high-end semiconductors essential for artificial intelligence development.
brief.why: The market volatility is driven by investor anxiety over potential regulatory tightening, despite previous efforts by Jensen Huang to keep sales channels to China open.

items.title: Jensen Huang Built Nvidia. Its Chips Made the AI Boom Possible.
items.author: Amrith Ramkumar
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has transformed the company from a videogame semiconductor manufacturer into the primary engine of the artificial intelligence revolution.

brief.what: Nvidia, led by its first and only CEO Jensen Huang, has pivoted its focus from designing semiconductors for videogames to powering the current technology revolution.
brief.who: Jensen Huang, the CEO and founder of Nvidia.
brief.context: Nvidia originally established its market position by creating specialized chips for the gaming industry before becoming the central hardware provider for the artificial intelligence boom.
brief.why: The company successfully repurposed its semiconductor technology to serve as the foundational engine for modern artificial intelligence advancements.

items.title: Massive atlas of brain region linked to a host of diseases is the most detailed yet
items.author: Miryam Naddaf
items.summary: Researchers have released the most detailed atlas of the basal ganglia to date, mapping 25.5 million brain cells across humans and primates. This project provides a foundational framework for understanding neurodegenerative diseases and brain development.

brief.what: An international collaboration has published a comprehensive atlas of the basal ganglia, detailing 25.5 million cells from humans, macaques, and marmosets. The study, part of the US$500-million BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network, identifies 61 conserved cell types and provides new insights into molecular signatures within the striatum.
brief.who: The project is a collaboration between hundreds of scientists across nine countries, led by the BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network (BICAN) and supported by the US National Institutes of Health.
brief.context: The basal ganglia are deep-brain structures responsible for motor and cognitive processing, and their dysfunction is linked to conditions like Parkinson’s, Huntington’s, and schizophrenia.
brief.why: Researchers aimed to create a 'massive dictionary' and a structural scaffold for the brain to better understand how cellular changes correlate with aging and disease progression.
brief.next: The researchers intend to use this framework as a scaffold to complete mapping the rest of the human brain.

items.title: Novel CRISPR therapy is poised to gain first FDA approval to alter genes inside the body
items.author: Heidi Ledford
items.summary: Intellia Therapeutics has submitted its CRISPR-based gene therapy, lonvoguran ziclumeran, to the FDA for approval to treat hereditary angioedema. If authorized, it would become the first gene-editing treatment administered directly inside the human body.

brief.what: Intellia Therapeutics is seeking FDA approval for lonvoguran ziclumeran (lonvo-z), a CRISPR-Cas9 therapy designed to treat hereditary angioedema by disabling a protein-producing gene in the liver. Unlike the currently approved CRISPR treatment, Casgevy, which requires removing and re-infusing cells, lonvo-z is delivered directly into the patient's body in a one-day procedure.
brief.who: Intellia Therapeutics is the developer of the therapy, led by CEO John Leonard, while the FDA acts as the regulatory body evaluating the application.
brief.context: Current CRISPR therapies, such as Casgevy for sickle cell anemia and ß-thalassemia, are ex vivo, meaning they require complex cell extraction, laboratory editing, and chemotherapy for the patient. In vivo treatments like lonvo-z aim to simplify this process by using fatty particles to deliver gene-editing components directly to the liver.
brief.why: The therapy aims to provide a long-term solution for hereditary angioedema, potentially eliminating the need for lifelong medication to manage swelling attacks. According to specialist Jonathan Bernstein, the four-year efficacy data is reassuring for the long-term viability of the approach.
brief.next: The FDA is expected to issue a decision on the approval of lonvo-z by 10 March.
